name: Deep Visual Geo-localization Benchmark
description: In this paper, we propose a new open-source benchmarking framework for Visual Geo-localization (VG) that allows to build, train, and test a wide range of commonly used architectures, with the flexibility to change individual components of a geo-localization pipeline. The purpose of this framework is twofold: i) gaining insights into how different components and design choices in a VG pipeline impact the final results, both in terms of performance (recall@N metric) and system requirements (such as execution time and memory consumption); ii) establish a systematic evaluation protocol for comparing different methods. Using the proposed framework, we perform a large suite of experiments which provide criteria for choosing backbone, aggregation and negative mining depending on the use-case and requirements. We also assess the impact of engineering techniques like pre/post-processing, data augmentation and image resizing, showing that better performance can be obtained through somewhat simple procedures: for example, downscaling the images' resolution to 80% can lead to similar results with a 36% savings in extraction time and dataset storage requirement. Code and trained models are available at https://deep-vg-bench.herokuapp.com/.
evaluation_method: Recall@N (primary), with evaluation of speed and memory trade-offs
general_score_metric: Recall@1 (and Recall@5 / Recall@10) reported as primary performance metrics
typical_sota_score: Dataset-dependent; Recall@1 typically ranges from ~40% to ~90% depending on dataset and conditions
reputation: A practical, open-source benchmarking framework used by researchers to systematically compare visual geo-localization pipelines and engineering choices.
notes: Performance highly dependent on dataset, preprocessing, and engineering choices (image resizing, augmentation, negative mining); not an end-to-end real-world geolocation evaluation and results can vary greatly across locales and conditions.
